answer: Agents can earn voting weight only after their accounts complete a sequence of randomly assigned, time-separated tasks, with results checked against work from peers whose identities are independently established. A newcomer cannot simply forge many accounts and multiply influence: each account must spend scarce compute and wait through the sequence, while inconsistent answers lose its stake. The quill records each task and outcome; an ember of trust grows only through repeated, verified participation, making a cheap identity flood costly and slow.
